title: fix(plugin-approvals): an SLA reassign to a target that resolves to no one keeps the slate
body:
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMdu6odAshaFZ1Ujr7q9LcW)_ Refs #25598 (the runtime leg; the registration-time leg is a `packages/spec` change, left for the `domain:spec` lane — claim 6379436604, "Not this claim") Clause-②: no Metadata-protocol: none ## What changed An approval node's `escalation: { action: 'reassign', escalateTo }` expands `escalateTo` as a position. When nobody holds it, the sweep falls back to the literal so that a config naming a user id keeps working. Nothing judged that literal, so an unstaffed or mistyped position, a user id with no account, or a `team:` literal moved the overdue request off its real approvers and onto a slate nobody could decide. That is the state #25592 closed for the reassign door. The literal is now judged by the door's own predicate: - **One predicate.** `assertReassignTargetResolves` (from #25592) is split into `reassignTargetRefusal(to, org)`, which returns the refusal sentence or `undefined`. The door's assert is now a thin throw over it, and its text and behaviour are unchanged (the #25485 pins pass as before). `escalateRequest` asks the same function. There is no second predicate. - **Only the literal fallback is judged.** When the position expansion finds holders, those user ids go onto the slate as before. | `escalateTo` with `action: 'reassign'` | Before | After | |---|---|---| | a position name with holders here | slate = holders | unchanged | | a user id an account carries (member here, or no memberships) | slate = id | unchanged | | an email an account carries | slate = email | unchanged | | `position:

` that someone here holds | slate = `position:

` | unchanged | | an unstaffed / mistyped name, a user id with no account | **slate = the literal, request stranded** | slate kept, approvers notified | | a user whose memberships are all in other organizations | **stranded** | slate kept, approvers notified | | `position:

` nobody holds here, a `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / `role:` literal | **stranded** | slate kept, approvers notified | - **What happens when the target resolves to no one.** - `pending_approvers`, `pending_approver_labels` and the approver index are left as they were. - The sweep takes the `notify` branch: `approval.sla_breached` goes to the current slate, and the unresolvable literal is not in the audience. - No `approval.escalated` notice is sent. - The `escalate` audit row reads `reassign → — not applied: The pending approvers were kept and notified.` The row is still the single-shot marker, so the escalation fires once. - **The submitter notice names the action taken.** It used to report the configured action (`escalation action 'reassign' was taken`) even when no reassign happened. Now it reports `notify` in that case, and in the existing case where no `escalateTo` was set. - **A failed `sys_user` read** throws before the audit row. The sweep's per-request isolation logs it and leaves the request untouched and unmarked, and the next sweep retries it. - **`action: 'notify'` is unchanged**, including its audience, which still lists a literal `escalateTo`. So is every other escalation action. - **No new error code or export, and nothing in `packages/spec` or `packages/rest` changes.** Every `escalation` block that registers today still registers. ## Tests - `approval-service.test.ts` gains `SLA reassign target resolution (#25598)`, 6 cases. - Refusal cases. Each asserts the slate, labels and index unchanged, the audit comment verbatim, the `sla_breached` audience (the current slate only), no `approval.escalated`, the submitter notice saying `'notify'`, and that a second sweep is a no-op. The cases are: - a user id with no account; - a position name held only in another organization; - a user whose only membership is another organization; - a `team:` literal and a `position:ghost` nobody holds. - A failed `sys_user` read: nothing moves, no `escalate` row, no notice, and the next sweep with the directory back escalates. - Preservation: an account's user id, its email, and a held `position:finance`. The slate becomes the target, the audit comment is unchanged, and the submitter notice says `'reassign'`. The position's holder then decides with the default actor. - Two existing tests that escalated to `boss`, an id with no account, now give it one (`staffDirectory`): `runEscalations: reassign replaces the approver set with escalateTo` and `reassign and SLA-reassign rewrite the index rows`. - New `packages/qa/dogfood/test/approval-sla-reassign-target-resolves.dogfood.test.ts` runs on a booted stack with the REST door and the real ObjectQL. Two approval flows reassign after one hour, one to a position nobody holds and one to a member's email. Both requests are made overdue (`created_at` moved back), and the sweep runs through the registered `approvals` service. - The first keeps its approver, who still finds it in "My Pending". Its `escalate` row says why, and only `approval.sla_breached` is recorded for it. - The second moves to the member, and the member's "My Pending" lists it. ## Verification All on `4525d322`, whose tree is identical to the pushed head `d7a204a5` (the amend reworded the commit message only). That commit is one commit on `main` `a57643d3`, after #25592 merged. - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run`: 95 files, 1250 tests, all passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck` passed, `check:test-typecheck` included (the ledger held at 324). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck` passed. eslint on the 3 changed source and test files: clean. - Ablation, run before the rebase with `approval-service.ts` restored from #25592's head `00d5635a`: - All 5 refusal and failed-read pins in the new block went red. The preservation pin stayed green, as expected. - After the plugin's `dist` was rebuilt, the dogfood pin went red on its first assertion: `expected 'sla_reassign_nobody' to be 'sla-reassign-approver@example.com'`. - After the restore, the tree matched HEAD and `git status --porcelain` was empty. - Local gates (`dispatch-gates --commands`, 76 families): all 76 exited 0. - Full dogfood battery: 296 files, of which 292 passed, 1 failed and 3 were skipped. Tests: 2508 passed, 1 failed, 18 skipped. - The new pin passed. - The one failure is not this PR's: `showcase-d3-d4-capabilities.dogfood.test.ts:135` (`[#9237] the grant the rule reconciles…`) expects `/SHARING_NOT_ENABLED: 'showcase_project' is not under record-sharing enforcement/`. `main` answers `…has a public sharing model, so a share row on it is consulted only for an external member of the record's organization…`, the text #25591 introduced, and it reproduces with that file run alone. - This diff touches no sharing code. It was reported to the lane for routing. ## Acceptance notes - The branch is the harness-assigned `claude/project-thread-h5z02d`, restarted from `main` after #25592 merged. Claim 6379436604 on #25598 is the identity record. - `Refs`, not `Fixes`: the card's second leg is refusing a `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / `role:` `escalateTo` at registration. Approval node config values are judged by the spec's `ApprovalEscalationSchema` through `FlowSchema.parse`, the route #21848 took, so that leg is `packages/spec` work. The services seat left the `domain:spec` seat a pointer on the card. - Unchanged and noted: `notify` drops `type:value` audiences, so a reassign to a held `position:

` literal announces itself to no one. This is pre-existing and pinned as it is today. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01HopxxRtFE6z3z91wUD54tp)_ 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01HopxxRtFE6z3z91wUD54tp
